I'm selling my small business after 20
years. The sale closes in about 4 weeks and the buyer wants me to like tell my
team 2 weeks before closing. I have 100 employees. Some of them are going to be
pretty annoyed. How do I break this news without it blowing up?
>> This is such a good question. I've obviously sold different companies in
the past and I've done it the wrong way and the right way. The wrong way I did
it was I gave a month heads up, which is exactly what you were talking about and
I wanted to make sure everyone was at ease and guess what happened? One,
people were not at ease. Two, I made promises because the buyer said they're
going to keep everyone in place. So I assured everyone that was what's going
to happen and then sure enough the buyer came in and then cut a bunch of roles,
changed the comp structure. It was an absolute disaster. The second time I
learned from that mistake because you never want to give the buyer any
leverage because if you tell your company 4 weeks or even 2 weeks before
the deal's done, the deal's not done. Like deals fall apart all the time in
the last 2 weeks. So as far as you're concerned, you're just creating fear for
something that hasn't even happened yet. Once the deal is closed, once the wire
hits your account, is when you then let everyone know about it. And then don't
make promises that you can't keep or that are not within your control. And
when you do give the news, the news is not hey, I sold the company, deuces,
right? Instead it's hey, we got to the company to the edge of my competence and
so what I'm doing is bringing in somebody from the outside who knows to
take the business from where it is to where I think it's possible and capable
of. And I owe to you guys, my team, to have as much growth opportunity as
humanly possible. And so this is great news. We're getting investment from the
outside to help us grow out. Because at the end of the day, you're probably not
selling a business because it's bad, probably selling it because it's good,
which means the future can be better with a better capitalized partner that
is more experienced getting to where you're trying to go than you do. Here's
the news report of my announcement when I sold my company. I wasn't expecting
that. Because I've done it.
